title: Find Median from Data Stream
keyIdea: Two heaps: maxi (max-heap) holds the smaller half, mini (min-heap) the bigger half, sizes equal or off by one. The median is a top or the average of both tops. On add, decide the side by comparing with the current median, and move a top across when a side would get two bigger.

approaches.name: Sorted array, insert in place
approaches.idea: Keep all numbers sorted; insert with upper_bound; read the middle.
approaches.why: Each insert shifts up to n elements.

approaches.name: Two heaps (smaller half / bigger half)
approaches.idea: Three cases by size: equal → push to one side, median = its top; maxi bigger → keep or move maxi's top across; mini bigger → keep or move mini's top across; median = average of tops.
approaches.why: Each add does a constant number of heap operations.

options: The largest number of the smaller half

quiz.q: Why must the sizes stay within one of each other?
options: Then the middle one or two numbers are exactly the heap tops

quiz.q: maxi already has one more element and the new number is ≤ median. What happens?
options: maxi's top moves to mini, then the new number goes into maxi
O(1): it reads the stored median (or the two tops)
